title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a lecture-style recap of the generalized Eilenberg–Zilber theorem, which Grothendieck calls 'Eilenberg–Zilber–Cartier' (EZC). It serves as background for the divided-power de Rham complex notes and for building cup products and multiplicative maps between Eilenberg–MacLane objects; the next page constructs K(Z,i)⊗K(Z,j)→K(Z,i+j) via EZ.

Setting:
- X_** is an abelian object of a category, bisimplicial.
- N: A_** → A_.. (Dold–Kan in both directions) is an equivalence onto double complexes.
- ~ is the unnormalized associated double complex. N ↪ ~ is a quasi-isomorphism whose complement, the degenerate part D(), is homotopically trivial.
- Δ: A_** → A_* is the diagonal.
- ∫: A_.. → A_. is the total complex.

Theorem as stated: there exist natural (functorial) morphisms ψ: ∫N → NΔ and φ: NΔ → ∫N. They agree with the evident identifications in degree 0, and φψ ~ 1, ψφ ~ 1 via natural homotopies k and h, with 1−ψφ = dk+kd and 1−φψ = dh+hd. For two choices of homotopies k, k′, the difference is k′−k = dl+ld with l functorial, and similarly for h. This is the acyclic-models uniqueness up to higher homotopy. The same holds for the unnormalized versions ∫~ ⇄ ~Δ.

The traditional explicit choices, cited from Mac Lane, *Homology*:
- Shuffle map: (∫X~)_n = ⊕_{i+j=n} X_{i,j} → X_{n,n}. It sends x_{ij} to Σ sgn(σ) s_{σ(i+1)}…s_{σ(i+j)} s′_{σ(1)}…s′_{σ(i)} x, summed over (i,j)-shuffles σ ∈ Σ_n.
- Alexander–Whitney map: X_{n,n} → ⊕ X_{i,n−i}. It sends x to Σ (front-face power in one direction)·(last-face power, d̃^i = d^n d^{n−1}…, in the other).

Application: the AW map Z(X×X) → ZX⊗ZX composed with the diagonal gives the cup product C^i(X,A)⊗C^j(X,B) → C^{i+j}(X×X, A⊗B) → C^{i+j}(X, A⊗B), with (f∪g)(x) = f(front i-face)·g(back j-face). It is associative and non-commutative, but commutative up to homotopy (via EZ applied to the swap), hence H*(X,R) is graded (anti)commutative.

Marginal notes: a shuffle picture (paths in a grid) and 'A, B̄(A)', a pointer to the bar construction.
errors: The cup-product formula is written sloppily: the variables run over x_1…x_{n+1} but the factors are f(x_1…x_i)g(x_{i+1}…x_n), whereas the standard AW cup product shares the middle vertex, f(x_0…x_i)g(x_i…x_{i+j}). The sign (−1)^? is unspecified. These are notational slips, not mathematical errors.
The AW formula's indexing of front versus last faces between the two simplicial directions is ambiguous as written, but consistent with the standard map up to convention.
'H*(X,R) est anti comm.' should read graded-commutative, i.e. commutative up to the Koszul sign. This is standard terminology of the time.

ideas.what: Generalized Eilenberg–Zilber theorem: for a bisimplicial abelian object, the total complex of the associated double complex is naturally homotopy equivalent to the normalized complex of the diagonal
ideas.where_published: used implicitly in SGA4/Illusie, Complexe cotangent; no explicit Grothendieck text known

ideas.what: Uniqueness of natural homotopies up to higher natural homotopies (k′−k = dl+ld)
ideas.modern_name: acyclic models / contractibility of the space of natural EZ equivalences

ideas.what: Explicit shuffle (Eilenberg–Mac Lane) and Alexander–Whitney maps
Cup product via AW, associative, homotopy-commutative, giving graded-commutative cohomology
ideas.modern_name: cup product / E_∞ structure on cochains (first level)

deep.surprise_reason: Textbook material (Mac Lane's Homology is explicitly cited) recalled as preliminaries for a lecture. The only mild point of interest is the naming 'Eilenberg–Zilber–Cartier' and the emphasis on functorial uniqueness of homotopies up to higher homotopy, both standard.
transcription_corrections: '∀σ,σ' next to the φ/ψ diagram is unclear; likely '∀ X' or a quantifier over objects. It is not a permutation.
'x_{i,1}' and the sum 'Σ_{0≤α≤i} s′_0 s′_1 … ŝ_α … s′_i x_{i1}' should likely read x_{ij} (and x_{i+1,i+1}): an attempted shuffle formula, partially crossed out.
The shuffle sum condition reads: σ ∈ Σ_n with σ(α)<σ(β) for α<β≤i or i<α<β≤n, i.e. (i,j)-shuffles.
'degen homot triv' = D() (degenerate subcomplex) is homotopically trivial.
The marginal 'Shuffles' and '[n…] […]' accompany a drawn diagram of lattice paths illustrating shuffles.
'associatif' appears struck through or underlined in the image; it is the property of the cup product being asserted.
